For statistical analysis, you can use Lee's L statistic for bivariate spatial correlation analysis, or another appropriate method of your choosing. You are testing whether NO2 in one place relates to Gas in NEIGHBORING places.

Determine whether the two variables show a significant bivariate spatial relationship. Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- don't spend turns trying different import paths for them. Implement this directly using only pandas and numpy. If you test statistical significance via a permutation/randomization test, use at least 500 random shuffles -- fewer permutations can produce an unstable p-value that lands on the wrong side of the 0.05 threshold just by chance, especially when the true effect is only moderate.

Thought: Load data, filter NA, build adjacency edges where both boroughs present, compute Lee's L statistic for observed data. Action:
```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load data
DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2023_no2_gas.csv'
df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
# Drop rows with missing NO2 or Gas values
df = df.dropna(subset=['NO2_value', 'Gas_value']).reset_index(drop=True)

# Load adjacency
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)
# Filter adjacency: keep edges where both borough and neighbor in df
valid_boroughs = set(df['borough'])
adj = adj[adj['borough'].isin(valid_boroughs) & adj['neighbor'].isin(valid_boroughs)]

# Prepare data for lookup
x = df.set_index('borough')['NO2_value']
y = df.set_index('borough')['Gas_value']
x_mean = x.mean()
y_mean = y.mean()
x_cent = x - x_mean
y_cent = y - y_mean

# Build list of directed edges
edges = list(zip(adj['borough'], adj['neighbor']))

# Compute numerator and denominators
num = sum(x_cent.loc[i] * y_cent.loc[j] for i,j in edges)
sx = sum(x_cent.loc[i]**2 for i,j in edges)
sy = sum(y_cent.loc[j]**2 for i,j in edges)
L_obs = num / np.sqrt(sx * sy)

print("Observed Lee's L:", L_obs)
```

Thought: Perform 1000 permutations, recompute Lee's L each time, calculate two-sided p-value.  
Action:
```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load data
DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2023_no2_gas.csv'
df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH).dropna(subset=['NO2_value', 'Gas_value']).reset_index(drop=True)

# Load adjacency
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)
valid = set(df['borough'])
adj = adj[adj['borough'].isin(valid) & adj['neighbor'].isin(valid)]

# Prepare series
x = df.set_index('borough')['NO2_value']
y = df.set_index('borough')['Gas_value']
x_cent = x - x.mean()
y_cent = y - y.mean()

# Edges list
edges = list(zip(adj['borough'], adj['neighbor']))

# Precompute sx
sx = sum(x_cent.loc[i]**2 for i,j in edges)

# Observed L
num_obs = sum(x_cent.loc[i]*y_cent.loc[j] for i,j in edges)
sy_obs = sum(y_cent.loc[j]**2 for i,j in edges)
L_obs = num_obs/np.sqrt(sx * sy_obs)

# Permutations
n_perm = 1000
L_perms = np.zeros(n_perm)
boroughs = list(df['borough'])
orig_y_cent = y_cent.copy()

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
for k in range(n_perm):
    shuffled = rng.permutation(boroughs)
    y_shuf = pd.Series(orig_y_cent.values, index=shuffled)
    # Map back to borough order
    y_shuf = y_shuf.reindex(boroughs)
    # Compute numerator and sy for perm
    num_p = sum(x_cent.loc[i]*y_shuf.loc[j] for i,j in edges)
    sy_p = sum(y_shuf.loc[j]**2 for i,j in edges)
    L_perms[k] = num_p/np.sqrt(sx * sy_p)

# Two-sided p-value
p_value = (np.sum(np.abs(L_perms) >= abs(L_obs)) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)
print("Observed L:", L_obs)
print("p-value:", p_value)
```
